newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BOC results solid despite strong pound.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BOC results solid despite strong pound.

text.p: British-based international gases specialist BOC Group Plc became the latest victim of a strong pound on Tuesday, blaming sterling for an easing in first-half pre-tax profits and sales.

BOC, which is the world's number two gases company behind France's Air Liquide, reported a million-pound drop in pre-tax profits to 216.4 million in the six months to March 31, while sales slipped back two percent to 1.93 billion pounds. The dividend rose 7.4 percent to 14.5 pence.

But stripping out currency movements, the group's underlying performance was solid. At constant exchange rates, BOC said sales would have been five percent higher and pre-tax profits up by six percent.
Chief executive Danny Rosenkranz told Reuters the results showed "a pretty satisfactory quarter and six months, very much in line with expectations".
The market agreed, pushing BOC's shares up 9 pence in late morning trading to 984 pence.
In the core gases business, sales and operating profits were flat at 1.388 billion stg and 199.2 million stg respectively.
BOC said the pound's strength was also affecting its customers in British manufacturing, with its performance in the UK market "flattish."
But its increasing focus on the U.S. and the booming North Pacific region continued to pay off, with the company reporting strong demand for gases in both areas.

Rosenkranz told Reuters he expected the proportion of sales in the Asia-Pacific area to rise sharply over the next three to four years, to the "mid-30s" in percentage terms from just over 29 percent at present. The group's efforts are particularly concentrated on Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand.

BOC, whose gases serve a wide range of industries including chemicals, semiconductors, welding and food, has to invest heavily in production plants close to customers because of the difficulty of transporting complex gases.
This means the group has heavy up-front costs which it aims to earn back over a 15-year period.

Capital spending totalled 359 million stg in the six months to March 31, compared with 324 million a year before. BOC said it expected to spend between 750 million and 800 million stg in the current year, up from 700 million stg previously.
Rosenkranz said a number of investments, notably in the U.S., were expected to come on stream in the second half which would feed through in improved sales and profits.

At healthcare, where the group specialises in inhalable anaesthetics and critical monitoring equipment, sales dropped nine percent to 226.3 million stg and profits were down eight percent at 26.1 million stg, BOC said the market had continued to be "tough," particularly in the U.S.

Rosenkranz said the troubled specialist vacuum business, which creates super-clean environments for the computer industry, had "a good half-year," despite a 17 percent drop in sales to 168.8 million stg and profits down 20 percent at 24.9 million stg. He said orders, which have slumped amid retrenchment among computer chip makers, had risen in the period.

Rosenkranz said the U.S. semiconductor industry was "very hard to read. In the next year to two years I think it will be choppy, but ... by late 1998/1999 I think it will be up and running, which leaves us quite encouraged".
